question_text: Which intermediate awards are available on the MSc Artificial Intelligence course?
reference_answer: PGCert Artificial Intelligence and PGDip Artificial Intelligence.
required_points: ["Name both intermediate awards."]

question_text: After accepting UEL's offer, how many days does an applicant normally have to cancel the student agreement?
reference_answer: The cancellation period is 14 days from acceptance of the offer.
required_points: ["State the 14-day cancellation period."]

question_text: Which levels of study are covered by UEL's Manual of General Regulations?
reference_answer: It applies to UEL courses at Levels 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, including courses at academic partner institutions.
required_points: ["Identify all covered levels and partner-course coverage."]

question_text: What is the standard credit value and study-hour equivalent of a postgraduate module?
reference_answer: A standard postgraduate module is 30 credits, equivalent to 300 student study hours.
required_points: ["Give the credit value and study-hour equivalent."]

question_text: Under the Mitigating Circumstances Policy, how many times per term may a student submit late without evidence?
reference_answer: A student may use the without-evidence late-submission route twice per term.
required_points: ["State the allowed limit for late submission per term."]

question_text: How many working days does a student have to submit an academic appeal after the relevant Assessment Board result is published?
reference_answer: An academic appeal must be submitted via UEL Direct within 10 working days from the publication of the results.
required_points: ["State the Stage 1 appeal deadline."]

question_text: What does UEL's Academic Misconduct Regulation mean by contract cheating?
reference_answer: It is work produced or commissioned by someone else, such as an essay mill or ghost-writing company.
required_points: ["Give the policy definition of contract cheating."]

question_text: Who must authorise a UEL award or distinction before it can be conferred?
reference_answer: The Academic Board must authorise the award or distinction before it can be conferred.
required_points: ["Identify the authorising body."]

question_text: How long does a student have to request a review after receiving the formal complaint response?
reference_answer: The student has 14 calendar days from the date of the Formal Complaint response.
required_points: ["State the Stage 3 review deadline."]

question_text: What is the maximum number of learning outcomes normally allowed for a 30-credit Level 7 module?
reference_answer: No more than seven learning outcomes.
required_points: ["State the Level 7 limit."]

question_text: When does the non-attendance support process begin?
reference_answer: It begins after a student has missed all scheduled sessions for 10 consecutive days.
required_points: ["State when the non-attendance process begins."]

question_text: How long does the industrial placement normally last on the MSc Artificial Intelligence placement route?
reference_answer: The placement lasts for one academic year, normally 30 weeks, including at least 24 weeks of delivery time.
required_points: ["State the normal and minimum delivery durations."]

question_text: What attendance level does a student need before progressing to the MSc Artificial Intelligence industrial placement module?
reference_answer: Students on the placement course normally need 80% attendance across all modules.
required_points: ["State the placement attendance requirement."]

question_text: How soon after graduation or earlier withdrawal may UEL delete a student's email and associated IT accounts?
reference_answer: No more than six months after graduation or withdrawal, whichever is earlier.
required_points: ["State the account-deletion period."]

question_text: Who normally owns intellectual property (IP) a student creates while studying at UEL?
reference_answer: The student normally owns it, subject to the stated postgraduate commercial-exploitation exception; UEL says it will not require transfer of thesis IP.
required_points: ["State the normal ownership and the exceptions that apply."]

question_text: What information about study time must a UEL course specification include?
reference_answer: The specification must show the contact hours for teaching, seminars or one-to-one work, as well as the hours expected for self-directed learning.
required_points: ["Identify both required study-time entries."]

question_text: After an award is conferred, how soon should the degree certificate and diploma supplement normally be provided?
reference_answer: They should normally be issued within 12 weeks of the award being conferred, once the course has been fully completed.
required_points: ["State the 12-week timeframe for issuing both the degree certificate and diploma supplement."]

question_text: How many credits must a student complete before enrolling on a Master's placement module?
reference_answer: The student must complete 120 core and/or optional credits.
required_points: ["State the placement-entry credit requirement."]

question_text: What overall mark is needed for a Distinction in a taught Master's degree?
reference_answer: A credit-weighted mean of 70% to 100% receives a Distinction.
required_points: ["State the Master's degree Distinction range."]

question_text: What is the deadline for an eligible Mitigating Circumstances self-certification application for coursework?
reference_answer: By 23:59 on the day of the original deadline.
required_points: ["State the Mitigating Circumstances self-certification application cut-off time."]

question_text: If mitigating circumstances are granted at first sit, what two assessment options are available?
reference_answer: The student may submit up to seven days after the original deadline or take the assessment at resit; in either case the mark is uncapped.
required_points: ["State both first-sit options and the uncapped status."]

question_text: Can a student appeal a provisional mark or grade?
reference_answer: No. The appeal process does not permit an appeal against a provisional mark or grade.
required_points: ["State whether provisional marks are appealable."]

question_text: Can the person supporting a student at an Academic Appeals Panel be a paid legal representative?
reference_answer: No. The student may be supported by a friend, including a Students' Union representative, but that person cannot be a paid legal representative.
required_points: ["State who may assist and the paid-legal-representative restriction."]

question_text: How should academic poor practice be dealt with?
reference_answer: Through marking and feedback, not through the academic misconduct process.
required_points: ["State the required handling route."]

question_text: When does using GenAI in coursework count as academic misconduct under the regulation?
reference_answer: When GenAI is used beyond what the assessment brief allows, including submitting AI-generated content as the student's own without adequate acknowledgment.
required_points: ["State the assessment-brief boundary for GenAI use."]

question_text: Who can revoke a substantive UEL award if a regulatory breach is discovered after it has been conferred?
reference_answer: The Academic Board may revoke the award.
required_points: ["Identify the body with revocation power."]

question_text: Whose signature appears on every UEL award certificate?
reference_answer: Every UEL award certificate carries the Vice-Chancellor's signature.
required_points: ["Identify the certificate signatory."]

question_text: How long does a former student normally have to complain about an event?
reference_answer: Within one calendar month of the event.
required_points: ["State the former-student complaint window."]

question_text: How does UEL normally deal with an anonymous complaint?
reference_answer: UEL normally takes no action because anonymity can make a proper investigation impossible. However, supporting evidence may lead the University to consider taking the complaint forward.
required_points: ["State the normal treatment and evidence caveat."]

question_text: How many assessments may a 20- or 30-credit module normally have?
reference_answer: It must normally have at least one assessment component and no more than two.
required_points: ["State the permitted component range."]

question_text: Within how many working days of the submission deadline should feedback normally be provided?
reference_answer: Within 15 working days.
required_points: ["State the feedback turnaround time."]

question_text: Can online activity replace attendance at an in-person session on a campus-based course?
reference_answer: No. Online-resource interaction does not count as a replacement for attending the campus session in person.
required_points: ["State whether online interaction replaces in-person attendance."]

question_text: After how many consecutive days of non-attendance will SERT typically consider withdrawal?
reference_answer: After 30 consecutive days, following a holistic review of attendance and wider engagement.
required_points: ["State the typical withdrawal point and review basis."]

question_text: How long can a student initially take a break from their studies?
reference_answer: Up to one academic year initially; a longer break may be granted only in exceptional circumstances.
required_points: ["State the initial study-break limit and the exceptional extension."]

question_text: If a student's withdrawal request is approved, what date is normally recorded as the withdrawal date?
reference_answer: The withdrawal date is normally the date the completed request form was submitted. For DfE-funded programmes, the student's last date of attendance is used instead.
required_points: ["State the normal withdrawal date and DfE exception."]

question_text: After which point are students normally not allowed to transfer course within UEL?
reference_answer: After the second week of teaching; a later request normally requires completion of the current modules before transfer.
required_points: ["State the normal transfer cut-off and later-transfer requirement."]

question_text: Where does the Student Code of Conduct apply when a student represents UEL away from campus?
reference_answer: It applies beyond campus in both face-to-face and virtual environments when the student represents UEL.
required_points: ["State the off-campus and virtual scope for student code of conduct."]

question_text: May a student allow another person to use their UEL student ID card?
reference_answer: No. A student must not allow another person to use their UEL-issued student ID card.
required_points: ["State whether a student may allow another person to use their UEL ID card."]

question_text: What should students do with mobile phones in the library or other designated quiet study areas?
reference_answer: Phones should be switched off or set to silent. Students should not answer calls or hold telephone conversations in those areas.
required_points: ["State the mobile-phone rules in quiet study areas."]

question_text: Who is covered by UEL's Generative AI Usage Policy?
reference_answer: UEL staff, students, third-party suppliers, partners and affiliates who develop, deploy or use GenAI technologies.
required_points: ["List the groups within scope."]

question_text: What kind of human oversight must be built into UEL AI systems?
reference_answer: UEL AI systems must include human oversight so people can monitor and validate impactful decisions and intervene to correct decisions when necessary.
required_points: ["State the required human-oversight mechanism."]

question_text: How often should UEL's Generative AI Usage Policy be reviewed, and who reviews it?
reference_answer: Each semester by the Gen AI Steering Group, with updates as necessary.
required_points: ["State the review frequency and responsible group."]

question_text: What is the maximum duration of an unpaid placement under the 2025-26 placement policy?
reference_answer: An unpaid placement may not continue for more than 12 months.
required_points: ["State the maximum unpaid-placement duration."]

question_text: What minimum daily stipend applies to an embedded academic placement at UEL?
reference_answer: A minimum of £20 per day for lunch and travel, for placements at UEL rather than at academic partner institutions.
required_points: ["State the amount, purpose and institutional limitation."]

question_text: Which insurance document should normally be obtained from a placement provider?
reference_answer: A copy of the provider's Employers' Liability Insurance, where required.
required_points: ["Identify the insurance document."]

question_text: Before starting the placement, what academic and attendance requirements must a student on the two-year MSc Artificial Intelligence with placement normally meet?
reference_answer: The student must pass all taught modules and the dissertation, giving a total of 180 credits. They must also achieve at least 80% attendance across all modules.
required_points: ["Pass the taught modules and dissertation, totalling 180 credits.", "Meet the normal 80% attendance requirement."]

question_text: What responsibilities apply to a student’s access card while they are enrolled, and what happens to it when their agreement with UEL ends?
reference_answer: The student must carry the card, must not lend it to anyone and must report it lost or stolen within 24 hours. When the agreement ends, UEL cancels the card’s access and the student must return it.
required_points: ["State the rules for carrying, lending and reporting a lost or stolen student card.", "Explain that UEL cancels access and requires the card to be returned when the agreement ends."]

question_text: How do the options for approved mitigating circumstances differ at first sit and at resit?
reference_answer: At first sit, the student can submit up to seven days late or take the assessment at the resit, and the mark remains uncapped. At the resit stage, the student can submit up to seven days late or re-register for the module with attendance, provided they have an attempt remaining and may pay any applicable fee.
required_points: ["State the first-sit options and uncapped status.", "State the resit-stage options, re-registration condition and possible tuition fee."]

question_text: What are the deadlines for making an initial academic appeal and for asking for a review if that appeal is rejected at the initial evaluation?
reference_answer: The initial online appeal form should be completed within 10 working days of the relevant results being published. If it is rejected at the initial evaluation, a review must be requested within 5 working days of receiving that decision.
required_points: ["State the initial appeal deadline.", "State the initial-rejection review deadline."]

question_text: How low must attendance drop, or how many consecutive days missed, before SERT intervenes with a formal review or non-attendance process?
reference_answer: There is no fixed low-attendance threshold, but attendance below 60% is considered for formal review. The non-attendance process starts after 10 consecutive days with no scheduled-session attendance.
required_points: ["State the formal-review indicator for low attendance.", "State the non-attendance trigger."]

question_text: What makes a student-initiated study break different from leaving permanently, and how long is the initial break normally allowed?
reference_answer: A study break pauses the student's studies for a set period while they intend to return. It can initially last for up to one academic year, with a longer break allowed only in exceptional circumstances.
required_points: ["State that a break is temporary and includes an intention to resume.", "State the initial duration and exception."]

question_text: How are UEL course specifications made available, and what main information must each one include?
reference_answer: UEL publishes course specifications online. Each one must include the course title, available awards, modes and duration of study, aims and learning outcomes, curriculum, admission and progression requirements, contact hours, and expected self-directed-learning hours.
required_points: ["State that approved or modified courses are published online through course specifications.", "List the minimum categories required in a course specification."]

question_text: What are the usual requirements for a placement year, and how are they adapted for postgraduate placements?
reference_answer: A placement year is a 120-credit module with at least 36 weeks of supervised work experience. Postgraduate placement modules run for at least two terms, with supervised work experience adjusted pro rata, up to the academic-calendar maximum.
required_points: ["State the placement-year credit and supervised-work requirements.", "State the postgraduate minimum-term and pro-rata adjustment."]

question_text: What do the regulations say about entering a Master's placement and about failing a module on reassessment?
reference_answer: A student must complete 120 core and/or optional credits before the placement module. A student who does not pass a module on reassessment may, at a board's discretion, repeat it once only.
required_points: ["State the credit condition for the placement module.", "State the repeat opportunity after failed reassessment."]

question_text: What is the normal size of a postgraduate module, and what are the Distinction, Merit and Pass bands for a Master's degree?
reference_answer: A standard postgraduate module is worth 30 credits, equivalent to 300 study hours. For a Master's award, 70-100% is a Distinction, 60-69% is a Merit, and 50-59% is a Pass.
required_points: ["State standard postgraduate module size.", "State all three Master's classification bands."]

question_text: What characteristics normally make circumstances eligible for mitigation, and what kind of impact on the student must they have?
reference_answer: The circumstance must normally have been unforeseeable and unpreventable. It must also have affected the student's performance, prevented them from attending the assessment, or stopped them from submitting by the deadline.
required_points: ["Identify the three types of assessment impact.", "State the foreseeability and preventability tests."]

question_text: What deadline and usage limit apply to the self-certification route for mitigating circumstances?
reference_answer: The student must submit an eligible self-certification application by 23:59 on the original deadline. The without-evidence late-submission route can be used only twice per term.
required_points: ["State the application deadline.", "State the per-term limit."]

question_text: Why can neither a provisional mark nor simple disagreement with academic judgement normally be used as the basis of an appeal?
reference_answer: A provisional mark cannot be appealed because it is not a final outcome. In addition, simply disagreeing with an Assessment Board's academic judgement is not, by itself, a valid ground for appeal.
required_points: ["State the rule for provisional marks.", "State the rule for mere disagreement with academic judgment."]

question_text: What should a student know when seeking Students’ Union advice before submitting an appeal, and how is an unsuccessful appeal formally concluded?
reference_answer: A student may seek Students’ Union advice but should submit the appeal without waiting for an appointment, as a late submission could be rejected. Partner-institution students cannot use this service. If the appeal is not upheld, the student is informed in writing and UEL will issue a Completion of Procedures letter as soon as possible, or within 28 days of the appeal outcome if requested.
required_points: ["Explain how seeking advice affects the appeal submission.", "State how an unsuccessful appeal is formally concluded."]

question_text: Which two uses of generative AI in coursework are specifically treated as academic misconduct?
reference_answer: Misconduct includes using generative AI beyond what the assessment brief permits and submitting AI-generated material as the student's own without adequate referencing or acknowledgment.
required_points: ["Identify use beyond the assessment brief.", "Identify unacknowledged submission of AI output as one's own."]

question_text: What factors can make an early citation problem academic poor practice, and how should it then be handled?
reference_answer: Limited academic skills or unfamiliarity may produce errors such as incomplete citations or minor unacknowledged copying. In the early-study circumstances stated, unintended plagiarism, self-plagiarism or collusion without premeditated dishonesty may be poor practice, handled through marking and feedback rather than misconduct proceedings.
required_points: ["State the early-study and lack-of-premeditation factors.", "State the handling route."]

question_text: What authority is required to confer a UEL award, when may a substantive award be revoked, and what must appear on its certificate?
reference_answer: An award cannot be conferred without Academic Board authority. The Academic Board may revoke a substantive award if a breach of regulations is established after conferment. The certificate must bear the Vice-Chancellor’s signature and record UEL’s name, the recipient’s name, the award, course title and any appropriate approved endorsement.
required_points: ["State whose authority is required for conferment.", "Explain when a substantive award may be revoked.", "Identify the required certificate signature and information."]

question_text: What information appears on an award certificate, and what additional study record can appear on a diploma supplement?
reference_answer: The certificate records UEL's name, the recipient, the award, the course title and any approved endorsement. A diploma supplement may also record enrolment dates, completed study elements with level, grade and date, partner institution details, registration place and language information.
required_points: ["List the core award-certificate fields.", "List the additional study-record information available in a diploma supplement."]

question_text: What are the normal deadlines for moving a complaint from Stage 1 to Stage 2 and from Stage 2 to Stage 3?
reference_answer: A Stage 2 complaint should be submitted within one calendar month of the written Stage 1 response. A Stage 3 review must be requested within 14 calendar days of the Stage 2 response.
required_points: ["State the Stage 2 submission window.", "State the Stage 3 review window."]

question_text: Why are anonymous complaints normally not acted on, and how is information handled when UEL investigates a complaint?
reference_answer: Anonymous complaints may prevent UEL from carrying out the investigation needed to resolve them, so normally no action is taken. If a complaint is investigated, it is handled confidentially and information is shared only with those who need it to investigate or respond.
required_points: ["Explain why anonymous complaints are normally not acted on.", "State that complaint information is shared only with those who need it."]

question_text: What must happen before assessment tasks are issued and marks are released in relation to the External Examiner?
reference_answer: First-sit and reassessment tasks should be approved by the External Examiner at least 12 weeks before submission or examination, and marks must not be released until the External Examiner and Assessment Board approval requirements are met.
required_points: ["State the assessment-task approval lead time.", "State the restriction on releasing unapproved marks."]

question_text: How should developmental feedback be presented, and what should students be told about feedback when an assessment task is set?
reference_answer: Developmental feedback should be specific, clear, constructive, relevant, actionable and forward-looking. When an assessment task is set, students should be told the nature and extent of the feedback they can expect.
required_points: ["Identify the required qualities of developmental feedback.", "Explain what feedback information must be communicated when an assessment task is set."]

question_text: What should a student do for an absence longer than five working days, and does online activity replace missed campus attendance?
reference_answer: They should contact SERT to create a supportive action plan. Interacting with online resources does not replace in-person attendance at a campus-based teaching session.
required_points: ["State when to contact SERT and why.", "State that online activity is not an attendance substitute."]

question_text: Where and to whom does the Student Code of Conduct apply, and what may happen if it is breached?
reference_answer: The code applies to all students at every UEL site and when they represent UEL beyond campus, whether face to face or online. A breach is dealt with under the relevant University procedure and may become a disciplinary matter.
required_points: ["State the groups and settings covered.", "State the procedural consequence of a breach."]

question_text: Which transparency and fairness controls does the GenAI policy require, and what human safeguard must accompany them?
reference_answer: The policy requires clear documentation, regular fairness audits, appropriate security and ongoing monitoring. AI systems must also have human oversight so that people can monitor them, intervene when needed, and correct errors or bias.
required_points: ["State the transparency, fairness, security and monitoring controls.", "State the human safeguard."]

question_text: What is the difference between self-certifying without evidence and making a mitigating-circumstances claim with evidence?
reference_answer: Self-certification allows eligible coursework to be submitted up to seven days late without evidence, subject to the 23:59 original-deadline application cut-off. A claim with evidence can support seven-day late submission or an uncapped move to resit if granted.
required_points: ["Describe self-certification, including its application deadline.", "Describe the evidence-supported options."]

question_text: What is the difference between an academic appeal and a student complaint under UEL’s procedures?
reference_answer: An academic appeal challenges or requests reconsideration of a decision about student progress, assessment or awards. A student complaint expresses dissatisfaction with something UEL has or has not done, or with the standard of a service provided by or on behalf of UEL.
required_points: ["Define an academic appeal.", "Define a student complaint."]

question_text: How does academic poor practice differ from academic misconduct in both cause and handling?
reference_answer: Poor practice normally arises from limited academic skills or unfamiliarity and, in the specified early-study circumstances without premeditated dishonesty, is handled through marking and feedback. Proven academic misconduct breaches integrity rules and is penalised under the misconduct process.
required_points: ["State the cause and typical nature of poor practice.", "State the poor-practice handling route.", "State the misconduct consequence."]

question_text: Under UEL's policy, what is the difference between attendance and engagement?
reference_answer: Attendance is in-person participation at a compulsory teaching session. Engagement is participation in wider non-compulsory institutional activity, online or physical, such as using learning resources, entering the library or meeting support services.
required_points: ["Define attendance.", "Define engagement and give its online/physical scope."]

question_text: How is taking a study break different from withdrawing from UEL?
reference_answer: A study break pauses the course for a set period while the student intends to return. Withdrawal means the student has decided to stop studying at UEL and does not plan to return to the same course; returning later would require a new application.
required_points: ["Define a break and the intention to resume.", "Define withdrawal and the no-return intention.", "State the reapplication consequence."]

question_text: How does the standard MSc Artificial Intelligence route differ from the placement version in course requirements?
reference_answer: The placement version adds a 120 P-credit industrial placement after the taught modules and dissertation; students must first pass 180 credits and normally satisfy the 80% attendance requirement before progressing to it.
required_points: ["Identify the additional placement module.", "State the prior 180-credit condition.", "State the normal attendance condition."]

question_text: How is cancelling the student agreement during the cancellation period different from withdrawing after study has begun?
reference_answer: Cancellation is exercised within 14 days of accepting the offer by giving a clear written notice. Withdrawal means notifying UEL that study is ending; it affects fees and, for visa students, is reported to UKVI.
required_points: ["State the cancellation timing and notice requirement.", "State withdrawal notification and its fee/visa effects."]

question_text: What is the difference between confirmed and provisional assessment results?
reference_answer: Confirmed Assessment Board outcomes are published through UEL Direct and trigger responsibilities such as engaging with reassessment. Provisional results may appear before Board ratification and can change until final ratification.
required_points: ["State how confirmed outcomes are published and used.", "State the changeable status of provisional results."]

question_text: What is the difference between providing alternative assessment modes as a standard option and arranging an alternative assessment for an individual student?
reference_answer: Standard assessment design should offer alternative modes where possible and permitted by PSRB requirements, rather than only when requested. An individual alternative assessment is considered only when the existing options, even with reasonable adjustments, continue to create barriers.
required_points: ["Explain how standard alternative assessment modes are provided.", "Explain when an individual alternative assessment is considered."]

question_text: How does the Merit threshold for an ordinary degree differ from that for a taught Master's award?
reference_answer: For an ordinary degree, Merit is 55-69%. For a Master's award, Merit is 60-69%.
required_points: ["State the ordinary-degree Merit range.", "State the Master's Merit range."]

question_text: How can mark capping differ when mitigating circumstances are granted at first sit versus at resit?
reference_answer: At first sit, using the granted option leads to an uncapped late submission or resit. At resit, if there was no previous mitigation on that assessment, the mark is capped under the cited undergraduate or Level 7 rules.
required_points: ["State the uncapped first-sit position.", "State the capped resit position where there was no previous mitigation."]

question_text: Why is a final Assessment Board decision potentially appealable while a provisional mark is not?
reference_answer: Academic appeals allow permitted challenges to final Board decisions about assessment, progression or an award. A provisional mark or grade cannot be appealed because it has not yet been finally ratified.
required_points: ["State the decision subject matter of an appeal.", "State the provisional-mark restriction."]

question_text: What is the difference between collusion and contract cheating?
reference_answer: Collusion involves jointly created work being submitted as one person's own, or one person sharing work that others submit as theirs. Contract cheating involves work produced or commissioned by another person or service, such as an essay mill or ghost writer.
required_points: ["Define collusion.", "Define contract cheating."]

question_text: How does plagiarism differ from self-plagiarism?
reference_answer: Plagiarism presents someone else's material as one's own without acknowledgment or permission. Self-plagiarism reuses work previously submitted by the same student at UEL or another institution in a different assessment.
required_points: ["Define plagiarism.", "Define self-plagiarism."]

question_text: What is the difference between an aegrotat award and a posthumous award?
reference_answer: An aegrotat award is an undergraduate award that may be made when the relevant conditions are met for a candidate. A posthumous award can be any UEL award and may be accepted on the student's behalf by an appropriate person; the Vice-Chancellor decides the level of the award.
required_points: ["State the aegrotat condition and undergraduate limitation.", "State who may accept a posthumous award and who decides its level."]

question_text: What happens at each of the three stages of UEL's student complaints process?
reference_answer: Stage 1 aims to resolve the issue locally and is normally completed within one calendar month. Stage 2 is a formal complaint made after an unsatisfactory Stage 1 response, normally within one calendar month of that response. Stage 3 is a review of the Stage 2 outcome and must be requested within 14 calendar days.
required_points: ["Identify Stage 1 local resolution's normal completion period.", "Identify the Stage 2 formal-complaint submission window.", "Identify Stage 3 review and its request window."]

question_text: What is the difference between the Mitigating Circumstances process and alternative assessment arrangements?
reference_answer: Mitigating Circumstances supports students whose studies are affected by unforeseen challenges. Alternative assessment arrangements provide another way to assess students who cannot undertake the standard assessment because of a disability, medical condition, pregnancy or relevant personal circumstances.
required_points: ["Explain the purpose of Mitigating Circumstances.", "Explain the purpose of alternative assessment arrangements."]

question_text: How does the policy distinguish low attendance from non-attendance?
reference_answer: Low attendance is reviewed holistically at set checkpoints. There is no fixed threshold, although attendance below 60% prompts a formal review. Non-attendance means missing every scheduled session for 10 consecutive days and may lead to withdrawal being considered after 30 days.
required_points: ["State the low-attendance review approach and 60% indicator.", "State the non-attendance trigger.", "State the later withdrawal consideration point."]

question_text: How does transferring to another UEL course differ from moving to a different education provider?
reference_answer: Moving to another UEL course is an internal transfer that follows the course-transfer process and requires course-leader approval. Moving to another provider is dealt with through the student-initiated withdrawal process instead.
required_points: ["Define an internal UEL course transfer.", "State that an external move uses the withdrawal process.", "State the internal approval requirement."]

question_text: Does UEL's Generative AI Usage Policy replace the University's assessment and academic-misconduct rules?
reference_answer: No. The policy provides an additional framework for responsible use and does not replace other policies or guidance. Rules for AI use in an assessment must be set out clearly and work alongside policies such as Academic Misconduct and Assessment and Feedback.
required_points: ["State that the GenAI policy is supplementary.", "State that assessment-specific guidance is required.", "Identify related academic policies."]
